pkg:ai/providers/compat-schema#ProviderC.rationale: Owner re-approved 2026-11-08 (the 2026-11-02 approval covered the 1.5.0 shape; compat-schema.ts changed in five commits since: a758f3ae4 supportsMessageThreads, 14b804d80, 0f4d5e960 promptCacheKeyMode, 7a6bd5a97 requiresToolsWithToolHistory, c5d397835; this text is the one approved, restated for Pi 1.5.1: compat-schema.ts is byte-identical at 1.5.0+c23b9ec1 and 1.5.1). Pi packages/ai/src/providers/compat-schema.ts:695 ProviderCompat: `ProviderCompat = Static<typeof ProviderCompatSchema>` is the models.json provider and model compat object. ProviderCompatSchema (:688) is openObject(ProviderCompatProperties, { additionalProperties: true }), where ProviderCompatProperties (:676) is mergeCompatProperties (:635) of every API's compat properties (OpenAI completions and responses, Anthropic messages, Bedrock, Mistral, System One) with API-agnostic overrides, and it allows other properties. PiG declares it as `type providerCompat ai.OpenAICompat` (internal/codingagent/model_registry.go:306). The OpenAI completions and Responses fields are typed members, and so are the Anthropic fields PiG reads outside the Anthropic compat struct: supportsMidConvoEffort, supportsMidConvoSystemMessages, supportsMidConvoToolAdditions, supportsMidConvoToolChanges, supportsMessageThreads (a758f3ae4), allowedFallbackModels, plus requiresNonNullAssistantContent, requiresToolsWithToolHistory and promptCacheKeyMode (ai/openai.go). Every other member, the other APIs' fields included (imageInput and sendImageOptInHeader of System One, the Bedrock and Mistral fields), is kept verbatim in OpenAICompat.Extra and written back in order (ai/model_compat_json.go UnmarshalJSON, MarshalJSON appends Extra), as Pi's compat object keeps an additional property. A member of another API is read from Extra where an API uses it (overlaySystemOneCompat, native_provider_composer.go) and the schema is the ProviderCompatSchema of internal/codingagent/configschema/compat_b.go, byte-equal to Pi's (configschema/compat_schema_exports_test.go TestCompatSchemaExportsMatchPi), so a models.json compat object validates and round-trips as in Pi. A member-for-member struct would type fields no code path reads outside their own API's compat struct (ai.AnthropicMessagesCompat, ai.BedrockCompat, ai.MistralConversationsCompat, ai.SystemOneCompat). The ProviderCompat object itself is a type-level view in TypeScript (a Static of a merged property map). Designed out so the typed fields and the verbatim members stay one object, as Pi's open object does. Re-reviewed at Pi c23b9ec1.

pkg:ai/utils/text#ownedSlice.rationale: Pi f715a15c1 and d8d99950a add ownedSlice(text, start, end?) to utils/text.ts and to chord's delta entry: `${text.slice(start, end)} `.slice(0, -1), a copy of the slice. V8 represents a slice of 13 or more characters as a view that keeps the whole source string alive, so an append op or an error excerpt cut from a long string would retain that string; the copy ends the retention and returns the same string value. Go strings have no such view-versus-copy distinction visible to a program (a substring shares memory with its source, a retention Go code avoids with strings.Clone where it keeps a cut of a larger string: delta.AppendText clones its text), and no Go behavior depends on it, so there is no Go function to port. Designed out as a JavaScript engine representation detail.

pkg:chord/.#Context.rationale: Pi chord/src/context/index.ts Context is the invocation-scoped value, abort and telemetry carrier (value(key), abortSignal, telemetry, toString). Go's context.Context is that carrier: the AGENTS async rule maps AbortSignal and request lifetime to context.Context, and chord/context supplies the typed keys (NewKey/WithValue/Value), the abort-signal helpers (WithAbortSignal/WithoutAbortSignal/WithCancel) and, since Pi 1402973a, the explicit telemetry parent (Telemetry, WithTelemetry, TraceIn) over it, a TelemetrySpan since Pi 2ec55d80. No Go type named Context exists or should: a parallel interface would duplicate the standard one. Designed out as a language mechanic (LEAD-RULINGS-1520 principle).

pkg:chord/.#Context::property:telemetry.rationale: Pi Context.telemetry (chord/src/context/index.ts) is the explicit telemetry parent of the context. Since Pi 2ec55d80 it is a TelemetrySpan, always present, where it was a TelemetryContext; it defaults to the no-op span. Go's context.Context has no members to add, so the carrier is the function chordctx.Telemetry(ctx), which returns a telemetry.TelemetrySpan (the no-op span when the context carries none, never nil, so a foreign context.Context reads as Pi's default and no Go caller narrows), and WithTelemetry(parent, span) derives a context that carries one. TestContextDerivesTelemetryIndependentlyFromValuesAndCancellation and TestContextIsolatesConcurrentTraceInBranchesAndPreservesCallbackResultsAndErrors (chord/context/chordctx_upstream_test.go) port Pi's two span-typed cases. Designed out as a language mechanic: a property of an interface Go does not own is a function over the standard context.

pkg:chord/delta#ownedSlice.rationale: Pi f715a15c1 and d8d99950a add ownedSlice(text, start, end?) to utils/text.ts and to chord's delta entry: `${text.slice(start, end)} `.slice(0, -1), a copy of the slice. V8 represents a slice of 13 or more characters as a view that keeps the whole source string alive, so an append op or an error excerpt cut from a long string would retain that string; the copy ends the retention and returns the same string value. Go strings have no such view-versus-copy distinction visible to a program (a substring shares memory with its source, a retention Go code avoids with strings.Clone where it keeps a cut of a larger string: delta.AppendText clones its text), and no Go behavior depends on it, so there is no Go function to port. Designed out as a JavaScript engine representation detail. Intention check (probe of Pi packages/chord/src/delta/index.ts:118): ownedSlice protects against a V8 slice view keeping its source string alive. PiG tests that intention in its own way: TestADiffsAppendOpOwnsItsTextAndKeepsNoRevisionAlive (chord/delta/owned_text_proof_test.go) asserts that an append op the diff emits is a copy in the bytes of no revision. A function of this name has no Go use, so only it is designed out.

pkg:chord/http#HttpComponent::property:u.rationale: Pi packages/chord/src/node/http/http.ts:97 `upgrade: (message: IncomingMessage, socket: Duplex, head: Buffer) => void` is the argument triple of Node's `server.on("upgrade", ...)` event: the request, the raw socket and the bytes read past the request head. Go's net/http has no upgrade event: a handler is given the (ResponseWriter, *Request) pair, and the connection and the bytes already read past the head are what the ResponseWriter's http.Hijacker hands out (the net.Conn and its buffered reader), which the websocket upgrader takes itself. HttpComponent.Upgrade(w, request) (chord/nextnode/http/http.go) is that adapter: an app's handler calls it for a request asking for an upgrade and it runs the same steps (refused 503 while closing, admitted, authenticated, checked again at hand-out, then the links endpoint or the plugin socket). Pi's intention (upgrades.test.ts): whichever way the app wires the event, an upgrade runs the same steps (refused 503 while closing, admitted, authenticated, checked again at hand-out, then handed out). The Node event triple has no Go form; the behavior is asserted by TestTheLinksEndpointAcceptsALinkAsTheAuthenticatedPrincipalWithTheOptionsLinksOptionsGaveThatSocket and TestPluginSocketsHandTheSocketAndItsRequestToTheHandlerInAScopeWithItsPrincipalNoPrincipalIsRefused (chord/nextnode/http/upgrades_test.go). Intention check (http.ts:96-97 read): `upgrade` is a TypeScript property of function type that the component's implementation supplies as Node's upgrade adapter; the behaviour is the steps the rationale lists, which Go's HttpComponent.Upgrade runs over a hijacked connection.

pkg:chord/http#nodeRequest.rationale: Pi packages/chord/src/node/http/node.ts:157 nodeRequest(message: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse): NodeRequest converts the pair Node's `request` handler gets, so that an app mounting `fetch` on its own server hands a Web `Request` (and the connection) to the component; `res` is there only so the request's abort signal is not raised once `res` finished (NodeIncoming.cancelled, node.ts:119-140). Go's net/http gives the handler a *http.Request alone with its ResponseWriter beside it, and the request's context is cancelled when the client goes or the handler returns, which is the same "not after the response finished" without a second argument: NodeRequestOf(r) (chord/nextnode/http/node.go; the Go function cannot share the type's name NodeRequest) takes the one request and answers a NodeRequest tagged Kind request or refused with the listener's own refusals (an absolute-form target 403, a target or `Host` that does not parse 400, userinfo in `Host` 403, CONNECT/TRACE/TRACK 501). Pi's intention (node.test.ts:84, node.ts:119-140): a mounted app converts with the listener's refusals, and its request aborts when the client goes, not before and not after `res` finished; TestMountedRequestContextEndsWhenTheClientGoesAndNotBefore (chord/nextnode/http/node_test.go) asserts the abort. A ResponseWriter parameter nothing reads would be a stand-in. TestMountingConvertsWithTheListenersChecksNeverPanickingBadTargetsUserinfoTRACERefused and TestReviewAGETBodyIsNoBodyOnTheListenerAndOnMountedRequests (chord/nextnode/http/node_test.go, review_test.go) assert the conversion. Intention check (node.ts:150-160 read): nodeRequest(message, res) calls NodeIncoming.of(message, res) and returns its refusal when it is not a NodeIncoming; Pi does not use the second argument for anything but to tie the abort signal to `res` finishing, which Go's request context already does, so Go's NodeRequestOf(r) takes the one argument.

pkg:chord/json#CopyJsonOptions.rationale: INTENTION CHECK: Pi's test (chord/test/json.test.ts "optionally omits undefined object properties without normalizing arrays") guards that a value that is not JSON never becomes JSON silently, that an absent property is dropped only where the option allows, and that arrays stay strict. The option itself has no counterpart because Go has no `undefined` (an `any` nil is JSON null, a Go value either holds a key or not), but the intention exists in PiG and is tested: TestCopyJSONKeepsNilAsNullAndRefusesNonJSONKindsInObjectsAndArrays (chord/json_test.go) asserts a nil member is kept as null, [nil] stays, and a func is refused as strict JSON in an object and in an array. Designed out only the omit flag. pkg:chord/plugins#RolloutStep.rationale: Pi 1.5.1 packages/chord/src/node/plugins/plugins.ts RolloutStep = {name, kinds, reload(built, context)}. PiG's RolloutStep carries the same name and kinds; its Reload has one more parameter, `applied`: Pi's step reads `plugins.current(kind)` in the synchronous part after its ship (no await between them), and a Go step cannot read that atomically with the ship, so the rollout hands the kinds' sets over (documented on the type). pkg:chord/plugins/runtime#PluginRuntime:.rationale: Pi 1.5.1 packages/chord/src/node/plugins/runtime.ts and plugins.ts: load takes a live Host (and core PluginFacets and live module values) that the runtime evaluates in its own process. A Go process cannot hand a JavaScript plugin host those, so PluginRuntime and Plugins start the Node subprocess host themselves (NodeHost, plugins_node*.go) and take the data of that start (RuntimeLoad: module files, Go packages, the host's options); Load returns the host and reloads address it by the Go handle. Intention check. protects: runtime.test.ts ('loading and reloading with complete sets': a failed build or evaluation is left out and reported with the host's report, same digests unchanged, a changed one applied, a loaded one not shipped removed, the loaded facet of a failing new build kept; 'required roots at load': a failed required plugin rejects Load with a PluginError after the host's load settled, a failed plugin of a non-required root is only reported; 'the runtime's imports': a worker that only evaluates never imports esbuild) and plugins.test.ts ('per plugin at startup' and 'at reload', the app's API and required roots, moved and removed plugins, 'fix round 1': reloads of one host serialized, a reload committed before an aborted wait is adopted, a kind its rebuilt facets no longer have leaves the plugin out, a structured clone reloads as the build, a changed package.json is read again, GC of old facets). pigTest: the same titles run through RuntimeLoad and the Node host, observing the host's load and reload reports and the facets the host holds: plugins_runtime_test.go TestRuntimeLoadsASetAndLeavesOutAPluginWhoseBuildOrEvaluationFailedReportedWithTheHostsReport, TestRuntimeReloadsACompleteSetSameDigestsUnchangedAChangedOneAppliedALoadedOneNotShippedRemoved, TestRuntimeKeepsTheLoadedFacetOfAPluginWhoseNewBuildOrEvaluationFailedAnAddedFailingOneIsLeftOut, TestRuntimeRequiredRootsAtLoadRejectsWithAPluginErrorNamingARequiredPluginThatFailedAfterTheHostsLoadSettled, TestRuntimeRequiredRootsAtLoadOnlyReportsAFailedPluginOfARootThatIsNotRequired, TestRuntimeLoadsNoEsbuildAWorkerThatOnlyEvaluatesNeverImportsIt; plugins_plugins_test.go TestPluginsPerPluginAtStartup..., TestPluginsPerPluginAtReload..., TestPluginsTheAppsAPIRequiredRootsAndInstalls..., TestPluginsFixRound1..., TestPluginsGCCollectsOldFacetsOver200Reloads...; plugins_endtoend_test.go TestEndToEndAServerAndAWorkerLoadsPluginDirectoriesRollsAnEditOutServerThenWorkerAndKeepsABrokenEditOldOnBoth. whyNot: the host-handoff form (Load(host, options)) needs a Go-held handle to a JavaScript host that this process does not run; it waits for the queued post-0.8.0 refactor, and the cases above stay the acceptance for it. pkg:chord/plugins/runtime#RuntimeLoad.rationale: Pi 1.5.1 packages/chord/src/node/plugins/runtime.ts `RuntimeLoad` ({kind, core: PluginFacet[], scripts, modules: HostPackages}) is the options of a load into a live Host, with live core facets and module values. RuntimeLoad is PiG's options of the subprocess start (Kind, Core as module files, Scripts, Modules as module paths, plus the host's Address, Principal, Peer, Heartbeat and timeouts) because the plugin host is started by Load itself, and a JavaScript facet or module instance cannot cross the process boundary (D607, D502). Intention check. protects: what runtime.test.ts and plugins.test.ts check of a load's inputs: core facets load before the plugins, the modules are the packages the scripts' imports are answered with and are kept for the host's reloads, the kind names the set. pigTest: every Load of plugins_runtime_test.go (pcRuntimeLoad builds a RuntimeLoad) and plugins_plugins_test.go runs through the Node host: TestRuntimeLoadsASetAndLeavesOutAPluginWhoseBuildOrEvaluationFailedReportedWithTheHostsReport, TestRuntimeRequiredRootsAtLoadRejectsWithAPluginErrorNamingARequiredPluginThatFailedAfterTheHostsLoadSettled, TestRuntimeTheHostsBackgroundErrorsCarryEveryFieldOfTheirKind, TestRuntimeTheHostsReadyTimeoutIsTheAppsAndAParkedAttemptIsReportedWithWhatItWaitsFor. whyNot: the host field of Pi's signature, and with it the live-value fields, waits for the queued post-0.8.0 refactor so Load takes a host as Pi does. pkg:chord/react#ExternalStore.rationale: Pi packages/chord/src/react/stores.ts (Pi 1.5.1): the React bindings' store adapter (ExternalStore, watchStore) feeds React `useSyncExternalStore`, which exists only in React. It is TypeScript that runs in the browser or in the terminal sandbox's JavaScript context; no Go process can host it. PiG ships Pi's file itself, unchanged, embedded in the server (chord/nextnode/surfaces/client: manifest.json records Pi's commit and every file's hash, `make vendor-chord-surfaces-client` regenerates it, drift fails the build), so the behavior is Pi's code, not a port of it (D601). Intention check: what Pi's tests for this module guard (the page or terminal follows the host's state, language and theme, holds and releases what it uses, and survives a base-bundle change) is tested in PiG, over the shipped files, not skipped. Behavior is exercised by Pi's own tests: node/react/stores.test.ts as chord/nextnode/surfaces/surfaces_react_test.go TestReactWatchStoresReadTheValueCallBackOnChangesGiveUndefinedForNoWatchable (testdata/react_stores.test.mjs over the vendored sources) and node/react/hooks.test.ts as chord/nextnode/app/app_web_browser_test.go TestReactBindingsHoldWhileMountedReRenderOnChangeReleaseOnUnmount, TestReactBindingsKeepPageStateAcrossARemountByANewFunctionANewKeyStartingFresh and TestReactBindingsReRenderMessagesInALanguageChosenLiveKeepingHalfTypedInputs in real Chromium.

pkg:chord/sync#FileResult.rationale: INTENTION CHECK: FileResult<T> and isNotFound (sync/files.ts:9-45) guard that an operation reports its failure as data and that a missing file is told apart from every other failure, which the remote relies on (a missing body is none, anything else fails). The intention exists in PiG and is tested: TestIsNotFoundTellsAMissingFileFromOtherFailures (chord/sync/lines_test.go) asserts IsNotFound is true exactly for fs.ErrNotExist, wrapped or joined, and that GetBatch of a missing slot returns none without a failure. Only the data-carrying union has no Go form: the (T, error) results carry it. chord/src/sync/files.ts:9 FileResult<T> is `{ ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: Error }`, the outcome of a Promise-returning file operation reported as data. Go spells that outcome as the (T, error) results of the call, the language's form of a value-or-error result: SyncFileSystem and SyncFileReader methods return (T, error), and a missing file or directory is an error that is fs.ErrNotExist (IsNotFound) where Pi tests `code: "not_found"` (chord/sync/files.go). The detector's rule S13f reads every call that returns FileResult<T> as the Go results (T, error). Intention check (files.ts:7-8 read): FileResult is a TypeScript union alias (type-level) of { ok: true; value } and { ok: false; error }; isNotFound (files.ts:44-46) reads `error.code === "not_found"`, which Go's (value, error) results and IsNotFound(fs.ErrNotExist) carry.

pkg:codemode/.#CodemodeRemoteExchange::c.rationale: Pi remote.ts:62-67 CodemodeRemoteExchange = (messages) => Promise<CodemodeRemoteReply | null> is one function of the messages that returns a TypeScript Promise of the reply. Go RemoteExchange(ctx, messages, reply) adds the context that carries AbortSignal and request lifetime and a reply callback that exchange calls exactly once: the Go mapping of a Promise the caller does not await before going on (remote_types.go doc: the messages are delivered in call order before exchange returns, the reply settles later, an error is a rejected Promise, nil is upstream's null). A one-parameter blocking Go function cannot deliver in call order and also return the reply later. Designed out as a language mechanic with this citation (lead ruling 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT); locked by TestAnExchangeIsAnsweredWithTheResultOfItsCall, TestAnImmediateToolAnswerReachesTheRemote, TestASynchronousToolAnswerReachesTheRemote and TestARemoteExecutedByHandReportsTheScriptThroughTheExchange.

pkg:codemode/.#CodemodeSandboxBase::cons.rationale: Pi execution.ts:363-390 CodemodeSandboxBase is the shared tool table, defaults and execution lifecycle; its public constructor(options, launch: VmLauncher) (execution.ts:372) takes the VM placement, and Pi's doc says subclasses only choose where the VM runs by passing a VmLauncher (execution.ts:355-356). The type name VmLauncher is not re-exported by index.ts, portable.ts or cloudflare.ts, but TypeScript is structural and portable.ts:20 and :35 export VmStartData, HostToWorkerMessage, WorkerToHostMessage and CodemodeError, so a Pi caller can construct the base or subclass it with a launcher of its own: (data, events) => VmChannel (execution.ts:58-76). Go has no class to extend; the placement seam a Go caller passes is a Remote for NewRemoteSandbox: Remote.Execute receives the same VmStartData (RemoteRequest.Data), reports WorkerToHostMessage values and failures through RemoteExchange (a failure reaches the host unchanged, as events.failure does; remote.go remoteChannel.exchange), receives each HostToWorkerMessage result as the exchange reply (VmChannel.post), and is stopped by a stop reply and the cancellation of its context (VmChannel.stop); the tool table, defaults, deadline and result handling are the base's, shared through the unexported newSandbox (sandbox.go). Differences a placement written that way sees: an error returned by Remote.Execute is reported as 'Remote sandbox failed: <message>' where a rejected Pi launcher is the bare message, and Remote() failing is 'Failed to reach the remote sandbox: <message>'; a placement that reports its failure through the exchange gets Pi's message. Locked by TestMalformedAndFailureMessagesEndTheExecution, TestAnExchangeIsAnsweredWithTheResultOfItsCall, TestAbortAnswersThePendingExchangeWithStop and TestRemoteSandboxHasTheToolTableOfTheBase, whose remotes are written by hand.

pkg:codemode/.#CodemodeSandboxOptions::p.rationale: codemode/src/types.ts:118-124 workerUrl locates the worker-thread entry file that runs the QuickJS VM off the main thread (a bundler or Bun-executable concern: the default is resolved relative to the module that creates the sandbox). Go runs the VM in-process under wazero with the execution lifetime owned by the Sandbox (sandbox.go), so there is no worker file to locate. By a probe, grep of .upstream/current/packages/codemode/src finds workerUrl read only by runtime/host.ts:354 (default defaultWorkerUrl()) and passed to `new Worker(options.workerUrl, { workerData })` at host.ts:194, so it has no behaviour beyond choosing the worker file. Designed out by the lead's ruling of 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT (language mechanics with no Go meaning are designed out with a citation).

pkg:codemode/.#CodemodeWasmModule.rationale: codemode/src/wasm.ts:9 CodemodeWasmModule = object types a compiled WebAssembly.Module opaquely because the Node type definitions lack the WebAssembly globals. Go has no host WebAssembly object: the module is its bytes (QuickJSWasm() []byte, or the []byte a SandboxOptions.Wasm loader returns), compiled by wazero in newEngine. By a probe, wasm.ts:8 declares `export type CodemodeWasmModule = object`; it is a type-level alias with no runtime member, and the only value of that type is what loadQuickJSWasm resolves (wasm.ts:21). Designed out by the lead's ruling of 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT (language mechanics with no Go meaning are designed out with a citation).

pkg:coding-agent/.#AgentSessionConfig::p.rationale: Pi AgentSessionConfig.extensionRunnerRef is the late-binding cell sdk.ts:333 shares between its callbacks and the AgentSession (agent-session.ts:498, 3644-3645). pkg:coding-agent/.#BashExecutionComponen.rationale: Pi bash-execution.ts:213 getOutput() returns outputLines.join("\n"), every streamed line the block keeps, and nothing in Pi 1.5.1 calls it (probe: grep of packages/*/src finds only the declaration; interactive-mode.ts records a bash result from the executor's result, not from the component). An extension that draws the component reads its own Node-side instance. PiG's block keeps only the tail window it draws, so a long command holds about 50 KB instead of its whole stream (33.3 MB retained after 32 MB streamed before the change). Keeping the whole stream for a getter no caller reads would undo that, and a GetOutput that returned the window would be silently believed as the whole output. Recorded as D176 (docs/additive-features.md, docs/parity/DIVERGENCE-IDS.txt; Locked by TestBashExecutionStreamingRetainsTheTailNotTheWholeOutput). ContextOutput returns what the block keeps, Pi's truncateTail(getOutput()).content.
The call row belongs to BashExecutionComponent.getOutput (bash-execution.ts:213), which is designed out: nothing in Pi calls it, and PiG's block keeps only the tail window it draws (D176).

pkg:coding-agent/.#SettingsCallbacks::pr.rationale: Pi 1.5.1 settings-selector.ts wires the settings selector item "share-destination" (auto, gist, radius) to the onSessionShareDestinationChange callback. PiG leaves that item out under D64 (docs/parity/divergences/D64.md, SCRUTINIZED:approved; durable correspondence 509f924dbd): its /share uploads to the PiG gateway for every destination value, so the item would change nothing, and with no item nothing calls this callback. SettingsManager keeps the setting (GetSessionShareDestination, SetSessionShareDestination) for a settings file shared with Pi. Locked by TestSettingsSelectorOmitsShareDestination.

The call row belongs to SettingsCallbacks.onSessionShareDestinationChange, which is designed out under D64 (docs/parity/divergences/D64.md, SCRUTINIZED:approved; durable correspondence 509f924dbd): PiG has no share-destination item to invoke it.

pkg:coding-agent/.#SettingsConfig::prope.rationale: Pi 1.5.1 settings-selector.ts SettingsConfig.sessionShareDestination feeds the current value of the "share-destination" item. PiG leaves that item out under D64 (docs/parity/divergences/D64.md, SCRUTINIZED:approved; durable correspondence 509f924dbd), so the selector config carries no destination; the value stays in SettingsManager (GetSessionShareDestination).

pkg:coding-agent/.#discoverAndLoadExtens.rationale: Pi loader.ts:828 discoverAndLoadExtensions(configuredPaths, cwd, agentDir?, eventBus?) hands the optional eventBus to every extension it loads. Go cli.DiscoverAndLoadExtensions(ctx, configuredPaths, cwd, agentDir) takes a context instead and no bus: the Extension Host runs each extension in its own process and routes pi.events between them, so a caller cannot supply a bus, and accepting the parameter without using it would hide the difference. TestDiscoverExtensionPathsMatchesPisDiscoveryCases, TestDiscoverExtensionPathsFollowsPisLoaderOrderAndRules, TestDiscoverAndLoadExtensionsLoadsWhatItDiscoversAndReportsFailures and TestDiscoverAndLoadExtensionsReturnsTheRuntimeTheExtensionsShare pin the discovery, loading and shared runtime. Recorded as D117 (docs/parity/DIVERGENCES.md, SCRUTINIZED:approved, number assigned by the lead).

pkg:durable/.#HookResult.rationale: durable harness/types.ts:612 `HookResult<T> = T | undefined | Promise<T | undefined>` lets a hook return a value, nothing, or a Promise of either. Go has no Promise and no undefined: a hook is a plain blocking function whose return is the value (nil for none) plus an error, the AGENTS async rule for an awaited Promise. The expandHookResult rule reads each hook through that shape. Designed out as a TypeScript/Promise mechanic.

pkg:durable/images#createPhotonImages::c.rationale: images/index.ts:39 `createPhotonImages(wasm: SyncInitInput)` takes Photon's WebAssembly binary because Photon is Rust compiled to WebAssembly and loads it through `initSync`. The Go processor (durable/images/images.go CreatePhotonImages) decodes with the Go image decoders and re-encodes with image/png and image/jpeg, so there is no binary to hand it and no argument whose value it could use; a parameter it ignored would be a stub. The parameter is a host-loading mechanism of the WebAssembly runtime (the same reason images/node.ts and images/cloudflare.ts exist), not behavior of the processor. Designed out; the processor is the native Go pipeline over internal/photonimage's byte-exact ports of Photon's codecs (probe: Pi images/index.ts read in full).

pkg:durable/testing#ExpectLike.protects: The storage and env conformance cases run independent of any test framework: the runner injects its own assertion hook.
pkg:durable/testing#ExpectLike.pigTest: PiG's own form: durabletest.RegisterStorageConformance and RegisterEnvConformance register the same cases with assertions built on *testing.T (durabletest.CreateTestingAssertions). A Go port of the injected hook was considered.
pkg:durable/testing#ExpectLike.whyNot: The hook exists only so a TypeScript runner's expect can host the cases. Go suites run under *testing.T, so the same property is held by the registered conformance cases and a second hook would test nothing new.

pkg:mcp/.#McpTransportSendOptions.rationale: Pi mcp/src/transports/transport.ts:9-16 McpTransportSendOptions is the options bag of McpTransport.send whose only member is the AbortSignal `signal`. By rule S1 an options bag whose only member is a signal is the Go call's leading context.Context, so Go has no type for it: Transport.Send(ctx, message) and OrderedSender.SendOrdered(ctx, message, placed) (mcp/transport.go) take the signal as ctx, and StreamableHTTPTransport.Send hands it to authorizedFetch, which does not dispatch once it has ended (TestStreamableHTTPTransportSendDoesNotDispatchOnceItsContextEnds, TestStreamableHTTPTransportDoesNotRetryRequestsThatWereCancelledWhileAuthorizationWasRecovering). Designed out by the tern lead's directive (chord-strict-120 Round 3: Send takes context.Context, no shim).

pkg:mcp/.#McpTransportSendOptions::prope.rationale: McpTransportSendOptions.signal is the ctx argument of Transport.Send and OrderedSender.SendOrdered (rule S1; see pkg:mcp/.#McpTransportSendOptions): it ends once the sender no longer waits for a reply, and the HTTP transport does not dispatch after that (TestStreamableHTTPTransportSendDoesNotDispatchOnceItsContextEnds). Designed out by the tern lead's directive (chord-strict-120 Round 3: Send takes context.Context, no shim).

Pi's `options` parameter (Annotations<T[]> & { minItems?, maxItems?, uniqueItems? }) is spread into the schema. Go has no optional parameter, and a struct of options cannot record the order in which the caller wrote the members, which the JS spread keeps in the schema (the key order is part of the provider request bytes and of fingerprints), so each builder takes variadic options applied in call order and typed per builder: Arr takes ...ArrayOption (schema/builders.go:48): the AnnotationOption values Title, Description, Examples, Deprecated and Default, MinItems, MaxItems and UniqueItems (schema/builders.go:180-186); the bounds are minItems/maxItems, not the string LengthBounds, as in Pi's own option type. Designed out as Go language mechanics (typed variadic options in call order; owner review flagged). The items parameter Schema<T> is the same index-signature brand type; Arr takes a Schema (`type` and `items` are written before the options, as Pi's literal writes them before the spread). It has no runtime value and upstream performs no runtime schema validation; telemetry/schema.go records that these helpers have no Go form. Go keeps the schema data and the runtime starter that takes the attributes (CreateTypedSpanStarter). Designed out by the lead's ruling of 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT (language mechanics with no Go meaning are designed out with a citation).

pkg:telemetry/.#createTypedMetrics::call.rationale: Pi's `schemas` parameter is typed `Schemas & ([DuplicateMetricNames<Schemas>] extends [never] ? unknown : { readonly "duplicate telemetry metric names": ... })` (telemetry/src/metrics.ts:124-130) over a non-empty tuple. The duplicate-name member is a compile-time brand that makes the call fail to type-check; it is never a run-time value. Go's CreateTypedMetrics(metrics, schema, schemas...) takes the first schema as a required parameter, the Go form of the non-empty tuple, and the rest variadically; a type-level uniqueness check has no Go meaning, and at run time later schemas override earlier ones as upstream's Map.set does. Designed out as a TypeScript type-level mechanic (LEAD-RULINGS-1520 principle).

pkg:telemetry/.#createTypedSpanStarter::.rationale: Pi's `_schemas` parameter is typed `Schemas & UniqueTelemetrySchemas<Schemas>` (telemetry/src/index.ts:349-352). UniqueTelemetrySchemas is a compile-time brand: when two schemas of the tuple declare the same span name it adds the member `readonly "duplicate telemetry span names"`, so the call fails to type-check (index.ts:279-298). The member is never a run-time value, and the function ignores its schemas at run time (bindTypedSpanStarter(telemetryContext), index.ts:352-355; 'no runtime schema validation is performed'). Go's CreateTypedSpanStarter takes the same schema definitions and likewise ignores them (telemetry/schema.go:139-143). A type-level uniqueness check has no Go meaning, and a run-time check would add behaviour Pi does not have: designed out as a TypeScript compile-time construct, the language-mechanics case AGENTS.md lists.
